rem:chirality-trefoil-electron-positron:
Remark Electron and positron words: a mirror pair. The electron is the word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (electron) and the positron is its mirror e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} (positron), the same word with every crossing reversed. The mirror word is the inverse braid, e^+ = (e^-)^{-1}. The chirality assignment is conventional. The physical content resides in their mirror relationship.

Where the chirality lives. The closures are the positive and negative Hopf links. Unlike the trefoil (the backup electron, which is chiral as an unoriented knot), the Hopf link is amphichiral as an unoriented link: its mirror image is itself with one component reversed. So the electron and positron cannot be told apart by the unoriented link type of their closures. They are told apart by the braid itself and by the orientation of the closure. The writhe, a well-defined invariant of the braid, is +3 for e^- and -3 for e^+, so e^- \neq e^+ in B_3. The linking number of the oriented closure is +1 for e^- and -1 for e^+.

Antiparticles from crossing reversal.

Antihadron construction reverses every crossing in the knot formula, \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. Mirroring yields the antiproton:

  \mathfrak{p}^{\sigma}
  = 
  [u^{\sigma}, u^{\sigma}, d^{\sigma}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H

Each quark is an unknot strand carrying one crossing letter: \sigma_i for u and \sigma_i^{-1} for d. Mirroring reverses the letter, so u^{\sigma} carries \sigma_i^{-1} and d^{\sigma} carries \sigma_i. The crossing energy of \mathfrak{p}^{\sigma} reverses sign. This yields Coulomb charge Q(\mathfrak{p}^{\sigma}) = -1.

Time reversal and the exceptional divisor.

Traversing the exceptional divisor of the brane tower reverses every crossing of the electron word. This maps e^- to e^+ = (e^-)^{-1}. The Feynman--Stueckelberg interpretation maps this to a particle traveling backward in time. The fiber adjoint involution acts on the weight decomposition and reverses the Reeb flow. Extending this involution to the exceptional divisor provides a mechanism for chirality reversal. The vortex tube reverses winding orientation passing through the blow-up.

Open questions.

  1. Vortex inversion: Reversing circulation of a vortex tube in the brane fluid requires translating classical fluid dynamics results on vortex reconnection to the categorical setting.

  2. Information transfer: Double chirality reversal (electron \to positron \to electron) constitutes a round-trip through the time-reversed sector. The fiber adjoint involution satisfies \sigma^2 = \mathrm{id}. This returns the system to its original state. Information preservation across this round-trip depends on the exceptional divisor's monodromy.

  3. The imaginary part: The Archimedean realization over \mathbb{C} permits a complex aether parameter q. The observability axiom restricts q to positive reals. A nonzero imaginary part contributes a phase to the crossing energy. This phase distinguishes particles from antiparticles without mirror reflection. The full theory models chirality reversal as a continuous rotation rather than a discrete flip.

  4. CPT from the categorical algebra: The fiber adjoint involution and the Frobenius structure derive the combined CPT operation (charge conjugation \sigma, parity reflection, Reeb flow reversal). The QOU involutive axiom implies the CPT theorem.
prose:intro-stable-nucleus-torus-knots:
For a multi-nucleon braid closure to resist spontaneous topological fission, its colour-tube trajectory on the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p \to \mathcal{S}_p must wind compatibly with the Hopf fibration. Links whose components fiber compatibly over the torus are the torus knots and links T(p, q), whose Seifert-fibered complements carry zero hyperbolic volume and therefore avoid hyperbolic volume tension.

This section defines the stable-nucleus locus, proves that torus–Hopf factorisation obstructs topological decay across the prime-power family T(p^n, q^n), establishes the left-projector chiral structure of the weak vertex, and proves the genus-4 uniqueness theorem: on Bring's surface, the Hurwitz genus bound and S_5 equivariance admit exactly two primitive torus-knot force carriers, T_{2,9} and T_{3,5}.
def:stable-nucleus:
Definition Stable nucleus (Skein energy minimum). Let \mathfrak{p} and \mathfrak{n} be the categorical proton and neutron (categorical proton, categorical neutron). The nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons (Z the atomic number) is the iterated Hopf link

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  = 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{p} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathfrak{p}}_{Z}
   \oplus 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{n} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathfrak{n}}_{N}.

The nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) is stable if (Z, N) is a critical point of the Skein binding Lagrangian \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} (Skein binding Lagrangian) under beta variation (exchange of \mathfrak{p} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{n} at fixed A = Z + N):

  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}}{\partial Z}
  \bigg|_{A}
  = 0 .

A stable atom appends Z electrons e^- (electron):

  \mathcal{A}(Z, N)
  = 
  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)  \oplus  Z \cdot e^-,

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. This block invokes real- and complex-analytic constructs, including real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, and numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities drawn upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:stable-nucleus-valley:
Remark The stability condition restricts the hadron to the valley of stability. Restricting the hadron definition. The abstract hadron (hadron) permits arbitrary multi-component composites. The stability condition restricts the physically realised nuclei to the valley of stability. Only configurations (Z, N) satisfying the beta-stability equation of the stable nucleus (beta-stability) are long-lived. Nuclei outside this valley undergo beta decay (\mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e or \mathfrak{p} \to \mathfrak{n} + e^+ + \nu_e) until they reach the stable configuration.

This is not an additional axiom. It is a strict consequence of the Skein binding Lagrangian. The parameter q determines both the strong binding (via (q + q^{-1})/2) and the Coulomb repulsion (via (q - q^{-1})/2). Their balance selects the unique stable (Z, N) for each mass number A.

Closed form of the critical point. The summary reading of the stable nucleus is a multi-nucleon Hopf link that extremizes the Skein binding Lagrangian. By beta-stability, its criticality condition is equivalent to

  Z = \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)},

where a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C and a_A is the Pauli coefficient. The letter Z is the standard nuclear-physics notation for the proton count, which frees p for use as a brane point.

rem:force-knot-identification:
Remark Force carriers from the involutive structure and saturating generators. The three Standard Model forces arise from three distinct layers of the torus knot architecture on Bring's surface. The saturating genus-4 generators T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} carry the strong and weak forces. Electromagnetism is not a knot. It is the involutive structure of the category itself.

I. Electromagnetism. Electromagnetism requires no dedicated torus knot generator. It exists in the \dagger-structure on \mathbf{C} and the crossing-sign decomposition of the Skein algebra.

The crossing energy at each site decomposes into symmetric and antisymmetric channels:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = 
  \underbrace{E_{\mathrm{sym}}}_{\text{mass (strong)}}
  + 
  \underbrace{E_{\mathrm{anti}}}_{\text{Coulomb (EM)}}.

The antisymmetric Coulomb channel reverses sign under the crossing reversal involution \sigma \colon K \mapsto K^{\sigma}. This implements charge conjugation C categorically. Electromagnetic charge is the eigenvalue of the involution \sigma acting on the crossing energy:

  Q(K) =  \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(K)
  - \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(K^{\sigma})\bigr).

This involution descends from three interlocking structures on Bring's surface:

  1. The \dagger-involution on \mathbf{C}. The positive-definite contravariant endofunctor f \mapsto f^{\dagger} defines observability. Every morphism carries a sign under \dagger. The electromagnetic coupling is the component of the Skein pairing that is odd under this involution.
  2. The complex structure on the color elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_z. The embedding \Sigma_4 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^4 induces a Kähler structure on Bring's surface. The complex structure J satisfies J^2 = -1 and determines the phase of the crossing energy. Electromagnetic charge is the winding number of this phase around the \mathrm{U}(1) fiber of the Hopf map \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1.
  3. The symplectic pairing on the color tube coordinates. The T-duality involution \iota \colon (X, z) \mapsto (z, X) on the symmetric cubic F(X, z) = F(z, X) exchanges color and spacetime degrees of freedom. The symplectic form \omega = dX \wedge dz is invariant under \iota. The Coulomb interaction is the component of the crossing energy that transforms as a (1,1)-form under the complex structure.

Electromagnetism is intrinsic to any knot. Every charged particle (knot with nonzero antisymmetric crossing energy) automatically couples electromagnetically. This structure yields three consequences:

  • Universality. All charged particles interact, regardless of knot type or genus.
  • Charge quantisation. Q is an eigenvalue of an involution, hence discrete (\pm 1 for leptons, \pm 1/3, \pm 2/3 for quarks in the Borromean decomposition).
  • Masslessness. Electromagnetism is not carried by a knot. The \dagger-involution has no Seifert genus, contributing zero topological mass.

II. Strong force. The knot T_{2,9}, the three-fold cover of the trefoil, carries the strong interaction.

The strong force binds by interpolation. The knot T_{2,9} wraps through all three color fibers in a single closed curve. This provides the topological rigidity that confines quarks into baryons. The three S_3 subgroups of the automorphism group S_5 of Bring's surface are the subgroups that leave one of the three T_{2,3} periods of T_{2,9} invariant.

This topology forces confinement. The knot T_{2,9} cannot continuously deform to separate the three color copies without breaking the torus embedding. Extracting a single color strand requires cutting T_{2,9} into an open arc. This is topologically forbidden.

At scales smaller than the color tube radius, the three strands of T_{2,9} are locally parallel. The binding from their global winding vanishes. This yields asymptotic freedom.

The torus knot T_{3,5} uniquely combines winding numbers from both families: m = 3 from the quark sector, and n = 5 from the T_{2,5} column. This cross-link drives flavor-changing processes. The weak interaction transmutes quarks between generations and converts quarks to leptons because T_{3,5} topologically connects both sectors.

Parity violation follows from the Skein asymmetry at q \neq 1. In the Hecke algebra H_n(q) a positive crossing is the generator \sigma_i = L_+, a negative crossing is \sigma_i^{-1} = L_-, and the smoothing is 1 = L_0. The Skein relation is the Hecke relation multiplied by \sigma_i^{-1}:

  L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0 .

Weighting the two crossings unequally separates the two eigenlines of \sigma_i. Let P_+ and P_- be the idempotents of \sigma_i for its eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}; these are the left and right circular channels of the Breit–Wheeler vertex. With [2]_q = q + q^{-1},

  q\,\sigma_i - q^{-1}\sigma_i^{-1} = (q - q^{-1})\,[2]_q\,P_+ .

The q-weighted crossing difference therefore acts on one eigenline only, and it vanishes at q = 1. Let W_L = P_+\sigma_i^{-1}P_+ + P_-\sigma_i P_- be the element that inverts \sigma_i on the P_+ line and leaves the P_- line unchanged. It is the generator minus this difference:

  [2]_q\,W_L = [2]_q\,\sigma_i - \bigl(q\,\sigma_i - q^{-1}\sigma_i^{-1}\bigr).

Both identities hold for every q with q \neq 0 and q + q^{-1} \neq 0. Which eigenline is singled out is fixed by which crossing carries the weight q: the mirror weighting q^{-1}\sigma_i - q\,\sigma_i^{-1} gives (q - q^{-1})\,[2]_q\,P_- instead. This one-sidedness holds at a single crossing. The Markov trace of T_{3,5} at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is not supported on the left line.

The following is a model statement without derivation. The weak force maximizes this asymmetry because T_{3,5} has the highest crossing count (10) among generators, and the q-vs-q^{-1} imbalance accumulates over these crossings. No computation here relates the crossing count to the size of the asymmetry.

Unlike the massless T_{2,9}, T_{3,5} gives nonzero mass to the weak bosons. Its hyperbolic volume is zero, but its 10 crossings generate crossing energy via the mass formula. The 10 crossings of T_{3,5} do not cancel. This yields the massive W and Z. This too is a model statement without derivation: the crossing energy of T_{3,5} is not computed here, and no W or Z mass is derived from it.

prop:weak-vertex-left-projector:
Proposition The weak vertex insertion is proportional to the left projector. Let \sigma be a generator of H_n(q), so that \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1 with h = q - q^{-1}, and assume q \neq 0 and [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \neq 0. The generator has two eigenlines: the line on which it acts by q, with projector P_+ = (\sigma + q^{-1})/[2]_q, and the line on which it acts by -q^{-1}, with projector P_- = (q - \sigma)/[2]_q.

The left line P_L is the eigenline on which \sigma acts with an eigenvalue of modulus greater than 1, and the right line P_R = 1 - P_L is the other one. For |q| > 1 this gives P_L = P_+. The weak vertex W is the element that acts as \sigma^{-1} on the left line and as \sigma on the right line:

W \;=\; \sigma^{-1} P_L + \sigma\, P_R .

The difference between the weak vertex and the free crossing is a multiple of the left projector:

W - \sigma \;=\; -(q - q^{-1})\, P_L .

This holds for |q| > 1 and for |q| \leq 1. Three consequences follow.

  1. The difference W - \sigma annihilates the right line, and it acts on the left line by the scalar -(q - q^{-1}). It vanishes exactly when q - q^{-1} = 0.
  2. An element a + b\,\sigma annihilates the right line if and only if it is a scalar multiple of P_L. Within the algebra generated by one crossing, "the right line does not couple" and "proportional to P_L" are the same statement.
  3. Let t be the eigenvalue of \sigma of modulus greater than 1, whichever of q and -q^{-1} that is, and weight the positive crossing by it. Then the weighted crossing difference is
t\,\sigma - t^{-1}\sigma^{-1} \;=\; (t - t^{-1})(t + t^{-1})\, P_L .

So the choice of which crossing carries the weight, left open in the force-carrier identification, is the same choice as the left line.

Scope at the level of a knot. The statement is about one crossing. It does not extend to the trace of the weak knot T_{3,5}, the closure of (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5 in H_3(q). Under the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the part of that trace on the right line of \sigma_1 is

\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\, P_R\bigr) \;=\; -\frac{q^2}{(q^2+1)^3} \;\neq\; 0 .

At the proton-anchored q_0 this is -9.33\,\% of \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\bigr). All of it comes from the two-dimensional block of H_3(q), since y_{(1^3)} = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1). For the torus words (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^N the right-line part repeats with period 3 in N and is never zero.

This holds for every trace with y_{(2,1)} \neq 0, not only at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Write a trace on H_3(q) as \tau = y_{(3)}\chi_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}\chi_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}\chi_{(1^3)}. Assume |q| > 1, so that P_R = P_-, and [3]_q \neq 0. Then \tau(x P_R) = 0 for every x if and only if y_{(2,1)} = y_{(1^3)} = 0. With \tau(1) = 1, such a trace is the augmentation \sigma_i \mapsto q; it already suffices that \tau vanish on P_R and on \sigma_2 P_R. Since y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2 \neq 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), no word-level one-sidedness holds.

Where the weak vertex comes from. The definition of W rests on two inputs that are chosen, not derived.

  1. The one-sided requirement. W is required to act as \sigma^{-1} on one eigenline of \sigma and as \sigma on the other. This is an ansatz.
  2. The side. The eigenline on which W acts as \sigma^{-1} is the left line, by the definition of P_L above.

Given the two inputs, W is unique: an element x with x P_+ = a P_+ and x P_- = b P_- equals a P_+ + b P_-. With J = P_+ - P_- and |q| > 1, the two one-sided elements are

\sigma^{-1} P_+ + \sigma P_- \;=\; q^{-1} J, \qquad \sigma P_+ + \sigma^{-1} P_- \;=\; q\, J .

So W = q^{-1}J, and the element with the opposite side, qJ, differs from it only by the scalar q^2. The Proposition above follows from the inputs and is, in this sense, close to a restatement of them.

What this does not say. It does not identify W with the physical weak coupling.
prf:weak-vertex-left-projector:
Proof Proof of the weak vertex insertion identity. Since P_L + P_R = 1, every element x satisfies x = x P_L + x P_R. By definition W P_L = \sigma^{-1} P_L and W P_R = \sigma P_R. Hence

W - \sigma \;=\; (\sigma^{-1} - \sigma)\, P_L \;=\; -(q - q^{-1})\, P_L ,

using \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h, which follows from the Hecke relation. For consequence 1, use P_L P_R = 0 and P_L^2 = P_L. For consequence 2, write x = a + b\,\sigma. If x P_R = 0, then x = x P_L = (a + b\mu)\, P_L, where \mu is the eigenvalue of \sigma on the left line. The converse is P_L P_R = 0. For consequence 3, expand t\,\sigma - t^{-1}\sigma^{-1} with \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h. This gives (t - t^{-1})(\sigma + t^{-1}), which equals (t - t^{-1})(t + t^{-1}) times the projector onto the eigenvalue-t line, and that line is P_L by the choice of t.

The knot-level value is an exact symbolic computation over the three Wedderburn blocks of H_3(q), with the z = q^3/(q^2+1) Markov weights y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2, and y_{(1^3)} = 0. The same computation reproduces \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\bigr) = q^2(q^{12}+q^8-1)/(q^2+1)^2.

For the trace characterisation, let \sigma_1 and \sigma_2 act on the two-dimensional block by explicit matrices that satisfy the Hecke and braid relations. Then \tau(P_R) = y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} and \tau(\sigma_2 P_R) = y_{(2,1)}\,q^3/(q^2+1) - y_{(1^3)}\,q^{-1}. If both vanish, then y_{(2,1)}(q^4+q^2+1) = 0, so y_{(2,1)} = y_{(1^3)} = 0 when [3]_q \neq 0. Conversely, P_R is zero on the trivial block, so the remaining term y_{(3)}\chi_{(3)}(x P_R) vanishes for every x. \square

prf:torus-knot-genus-four-unique: Proof Proof of torus knot genus four unique. Chern--Simons level from existence of the quantum observable universe

This makes \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}_{k}(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}) the modular tensor category. The numerical prediction specialises this shared object. It does not combine two independent quantities.

Conjecture (Chern-Simons descent correction, \kappa unproved). The fine structure constant receives corrections from the Chern–Simons invariants of the force-carrier torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} on Bring's surface:

  \frac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}}
  = q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q \cdot
    \Bigl(1 + \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{CS}}}{1 - \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}\kappa}\Bigr)

The correction tower \sum_{j\ge1}\delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\,j}\kappa^{\,j-1} is geometric with ratio \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}\kappa \approx 2.7\times10^{-3}, so it sums in closed form and has no truncation order to choose. The order-\delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^2 approximation 1 + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}} + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^2\kappa is its second-order truncation and shifts the sum by 11.06 ppb.

where:

  \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}
  = \frac{\bigl(\mathrm{CS}(T_{2,9}) + \mathrm{CS}(T_{3,5})\bigr)
              \cdot \tfrac{[2]_q}{2} \cdot \hbar_q^2}
             {q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q}

and \kappa = \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\mathrm{cl}} / \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{q} is the Gram determinant ratio of the classical and q-deformed Chern–Simons pairing on Bring's surface.

At the proton-pinned q_0 with the Witten-1988 value \kappa \approx 1.722, 1/\alpha evaluates to 137.0359351 with the tower summed to all orders. The CODATA-2022 value is 137.035999177(21), so the residual is -468 ppb. The value \kappa = 1.722 derives from the sketched Gram-determinant computation, which has not been completed. Exact matching at this pin requires \kappa \approx 1.9153, which differs from the Witten value by 11.2\%.

Of the two candidate causes — a wrong Gram-determinant identification of \kappa, or an order-\delta_{CS}^2 truncation omitting higher-order contributions — the second is now excluded. The tower is geometric with ratio \delta_{CS}\kappa \approx 2.7\times10^{-3}, so it sums in closed form as 1 + \delta_{CS}/(1-\delta_{CS}\kappa), and the omitted orders are worth 11.06 ppb against a 468 ppb gap — roughly one part in forty. Summing them makes the residual smaller but leaves it the same size. The defect is therefore \kappa, the quantity whose derivation remains unproved.

Proof sketch (does not close \kappa). The bare coupling \alpha = q^{-1}/([9]_q \cdot [10]_q) arises from the antisymmetric braiding eigenvalue. This is Layer 2 of EM coupling projection. It is normalized by the force-carrier q-dimensions from Layer 3.

The correction arises from the descent decomposition of the coupling endomorphism P_{\mathrm{anti}} on the force-carrier configuration. The torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} are non-hyperbolic. Their \tau-image geometric invariant is the Chern–Simons functional, not the hyperbolic volume:

  \mathrm{CS}(T_{m,n})
  = \frac{\pi^2 (m^2-1)(n^2-1)}{12 m n}.

The factor [2]_q/2 is the q-deformation of \mathrm{Vol}(S^3)/\mathrm{Vol}(S^3_{\mathrm{classical}}). It replaces \mathrm{Vol}(S^3) = 2\pi^2 with \mathrm{Vol}(S^3_q) = \pi^2 [2]_q.

At order J^2, the Gram matrix of the Chern-Simons pairing for the configuration (T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}) on Bring's surface gives:

  G_{\mathrm{CS}} =
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \mathrm{CS}_1 + \pi^2 s_1^2 / c_1^2
    & \pi^2 \ell^2 / (c_1 c_2) \\
    \pi^2 \ell^2 / (c_1 c_2)
    & \mathrm{CS}_2 + \pi^2 s_2^2 / c_2^2
  \end{pmatrix}

where s_i = (m_i-1)(n_i-1) is the self-linking, \ell = |m_1 n_2 - m_2 n_1| = 17 is the linking number, and c_i = m_i n_i is the crossing product. The q-deformed version replaces m,n with [m]_q, [n]_q.

The determinant ratio \kappa = \det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} / \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} --- of the 2 \times 2 Chern--Simons pairing displayed above, not of the 6 \times 6 Markov--Gram \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) of Frobenius Gram matrix, which is a different matrix and is singular under the production trace convention --- is conjectured to capture the self-dual damping at the J^2 level, with numerical value \kappa \approx 1.722. This identification is unproved. The Gram matrix is dimensionally ambiguous. Two sources of freedom were named here: the choice of basis for the rank-2 sublattice, and the explicit form of s_i, \ell, c_i in the q-deformed setting. Neither survives examination as an explanation of the residual.

The first is not a source of freedom at all. Write B for the change of basis. A Gram matrix transforms by congruence, G \mapsto B^{\top} G B, so its determinant acquires (\det B)^2 --- the same factor on both sides of the ratio, where it cancels. Hence \kappa is independent of the basis for every invertible B, unimodular or otherwise, so no choice of rank-2 sublattice can move it (confirmed numerically to 60 digits under unimodular, index-2 and irrational B).

The second is finite, and has been enumerated. Each of s_i, \ell, c_i and \mathrm{CS} admits two readings of the instruction replace m,n with [m]_q,[n]_q --- deform the composite, or deform its constituents --- giving 16 combinations, of which the shipped producer is one. What survives is the third --- that the ansatz uses the wrong decomposition, so that the pairing whose determinants are being compared is not the right one.

At the proton-pinned q_0, \kappa_{\mathrm{Seifert}}(q_0) \approx 1.90516 lies inside [1.8739, 1.9567] (0.53\% below 1.91531) and gives 1/\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} \approx 137.0359958, reducing the resummed proton-pin residual from -468\;\mathrm{ppb} to -24.5\;\mathrm{ppb} (+55.2\;\mathrm{ppb} at the lepton-pinned q_0). def:cs-gram-determinant-ratio:
Definition Chern--Simons Gram-determinant ratio \kappa. Let G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} and G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} be the 2 \times 2 Gram matrices of the classical and the q-deformed Chern--Simons pairing on the rank-2 sublattice spanned by the force carriers T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} on Bring's surface (Chern--Simons descent correction), both written in one common basis, with \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} \neq 0.   \kappa \;:=\; \frac{\det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}}}{\det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}}}.

A change of basis B with \det B \neq 0 sends each Gram matrix G to B^{\top} G B and multiplies each determinant by (\det B)^2, so \kappa does not depend on the basis chosen.

Conjecture Gram-determinant ratio \kappa as a Plancherel-weighted character product. Working over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}], let \beta_s = T_{2,9}, \beta_w = T_{3,5}. Each admits a Wedderburn decomposition into central idempotents of the ambient Hecke algebra H_n(R, q):

    c_\lambda^{(\bullet)}\; e_\lambda,
  \qquad
  c_\lambda^{(\bullet)} \;=\; \chi_\lambda(\beta_\bullet) \in R.

Then the Gram-determinant ratio \kappa = \det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} / \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} appearing in the Chern-Simons descent (CS coupling) is given by a Plancherel-weighted character product of the form

  \boxed{\;
  \kappa \;=\;
  \prod_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    \left[
      \frac{\dim V_\lambda}{\dim_q V_\lambda}
      \cdot
      \frac{[n]_q!}{n!}
    \right]^{c_\lambda^{(s)}\, c_\lambda^{(w)}}
  \,\in\, R.
  \;}

The displayed product is not yet a well-defined element of R, and making it one is part of the conjecture. Two points are open: T_{2,9} is the closure of a braid on 2 strands and T_{3,5} of a braid on 3, so the two character families live on different Hecke algebras and the product over \lambda \vdash n needs a common n; and the exponents c_\lambda^{(s)} c_\lambda^{(w)} lie in R, not in \mathbb{Z}, so the powers are not defined in R.
